mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases > 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative investor sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, reducing corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where GDPC1 declines over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strong economic activity, boosting investor confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases > 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) decreases by more than 100,000 in a month, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month, combined with a rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5%, signals a demand-side shock, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases > 10% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST decreases > 10% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 1% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure despite accommodative monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real final sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month, combined with a decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5%, signals a supply chain disruption, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and INDPRO decreases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where RSAFS increases > 1% and INDPRO decreases > 0.5% within a month.
